1.content: Assign a large positive bonus (e.g., +50) to any move that strictly reduces Manhattan distance to the goal. Assign a negative penalty (e.g., -20) to moves that increase distance. Additionally, apply a fixed penalty (e.g., -5) for moves that reverse the most recent action or revisit the previously occupied cell on the same axis, to discourage immediate back‑tracking.

2.content: Assign a moderate penalty (e.g., -10) for moves that would land on a cell adjacent (Manhattan distance 1) to a hazard. Keep a large penalty (e.g., -1000) for moves landing directly on a hazard. When a move strictly reduces Manhattan distance to the goal, allow the adjacency penalty to be reduced (e.g., halve it) or offset by the distance‑reduction bonus, so that necessary progress‑making moves are not discarded solely because they are adjacent to a hazard.

3.content: When the agent has performed several consecutive moves without any reduction in Manhattan distance to the goal (i.e., stagnation), relax the back‑track and hazard adjacency penalties: allow moves that increase distance or are adjacent to hazards to receive a smaller penalty (e.g., halve the penalty) to encourage breaking out of loops and making progress.
